results.question: How can I save money on S3 storage?
results.answer:
You can save money on your S3 service mentioned in F4 by using the following recommendations from FINDINGS and DOCUMENTS:

* Review S3 storage lifecycle rules to automatically transition objects to lower-cost storage classes or delete expired objects in your S3 service.
* Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically move data to more cost-effective access tiers when access patterns change, as described in the S3 Intelligent-Tiering documentation.

results.question: How do I lower my RDS costs?
results.answer:
To lower your RDS costs, you can reserve a DB instance for a one- or three-year term for RDS as noted in FINDINGS (RDS Reserved DB instances).

* According to FINDINGS, you can reserve a DB instance for a one- or three-year term to lower your RDS costs for 65.00 USD.
* According to the "RDS Reserved DB instances" document, reserved DB instances provide a significant discount compared to on-demand pricing by applying a billing discount to the use of certain on-demand DB instances tied to your instance type and AWS Region.

results.question: Explain AWS Savings Plans
results.answer:
Savings Plans are a flexible pricing model that provides savings on your AWS compute workloads in exchange for a commitment to use a specified amount of compute power measured per hour for a one or three year period, as described in the "What are Savings Plans" document. 

* Compute Savings Plans offer lower prices on Amazon EC2 instance usage regardless of instance family, size, OS, tenancy, or AWS Region, and also apply to AWS Fargate and AWS Lambda usage (from "What are Savings Plans").
* SageMaker AI Savings Plans offer lower prices for Amazon SageMaker AI instance usage regardless of instance family, size, component, or Region (from "What are Savings Plans").
* You can manage your plans, view recommendations, and purchase plans using AWS Cost Explorer (from "What are Savings Plans").
* Payment options include all upfront, partial upfront, or no upfront (from "What are Savings Plans").
* AWS recommends Savings Plans over Reserved Instances because they are the easiest and most flexible way to save money on compute costs (from "EC2 Reserved Instances").
